Minimum 2 years of professional work experience.

The Onboarding Representative provides comprehensive onboarding and employment support to prospective and newly hired employees, serving as a key point of contact throughout the pre-employment and onboarding process. Applies professional employment, staffing, and onboarding practices to ensure candidates successfully complete required employment and compliance activities prior to their start date.

Coordinates and facilitates onboarding activities, including employment verification, background checks, Live Scan/fingerprinting, required documentation, I-9 and employment eligibility verification, occupational health requirements, and other position-specific clearances. Reviews and processes onboarding information for accuracy and completeness, identifies issues that may impact a candidate’s start date, and works proactively with candidates, recruiters, hiring departments, and internal HR partners to resolve issues and maintain established timelines.

Interprets and applies University policies, procedures, and applicable employment requirements while maintaining confidentiality and accuracy of sensitive employee information. Provides clear, timely, and professional communication to candidates and campus partners, monitors onboarding progress, and ensures required tasks are completed in accordance with established processes and deadlines.

Uses sound judgment to identify and escalate complex or sensitive onboarding matters, collaborates with HR partners to resolve issues, and contributes to continuous improvement of onboarding processes and the overall candidate and new-employee experience.

This position may be required to report at different work sites including Irvine, Orange, and other locations. The incumbent must be able to provide their own means of transportation to/from work locations.
Working knowledge of organizational policies and procedures; knowledge of functional area and understands how work may impact other areas.
Working knowledge of the recruitment, screening, interviewing and referral processes.
Knowledge of HR processes and forms and knows organizational and departmental principles and procedures.
Knowledge of common software used within employment and other areas of HR, and how they work together.
Basic knowledge of employment law.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills as well as active listening and critical thinking skills.
Demonstrated abilities associated with problem identification; reasoning; ability to work with business units in the development of ideas to solve staffing issues.
Demonstrated analytical skills to conduct analysis and develop recommendations.
